newsitem.title: GERMANY: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS BACK-TO-BACK GIANT SLALOMS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-COMPAGNONI WINS BACK-TO-BACK GIANT SLALOMS.

text.p: Italy's Olympic champion Deborah Compagnoni enjoyed the bumps of an icy German hill to clinch her second giant slalom victory in consecutive days in the women's Alpine skiing World Cup on Saturday.

After showing composure to win her first race of the season in the discipline on Friday, the 26-year-old world champion kept her nerve and line through two testing runs to hold off Austrian rival Anita Wachter for the second day running.
The victory gave Compagnoni her third World Cup victory of the season and helped her stretch her lead over Wachter in the giant slalom World Cup standings to 40 points.
"I don't know when I am going to beat her. It is tough racing her," said the experienced Wachter, who has finished second in four of the five giant slaloms this season.
"My only chance of winning the giant slalom World Cup is to be consistent and hope she makes mistakes. Right now she is not making many."
Compagnoni clocked an aggregate time of two minutes 8.37 seconds for the two runs, 0.90 seconds ahead of Wachter, who had held a slim lead after the first run.
Germany's Katja Seizinger, the overall World Cup champion who disappointed her home fans by falling flat on her face in Friday's race, bounced back to take third with 2:09.87.
"I knew after yesterday how strong I was on this hill," Compagnoni said. "This is a good step ahead for me on my way to my main goal of winning the giant slalom World Cup.
"The difference between my racing this year and last year is that I manage the races better. I proved that today."
The race proved to be another triumph for overall World Cup leader Pernilla Wiberg, who took fourth, just one hundreth of a second behind Seizinger, her main World Cup rival.

Wiberg, who had struggled with her giant slalom form before the German races, still has a solid lead of 264 points over Seizinger in the overall rankings. The Swede has a superb chance to stretch her lead here on Sunday in a slalom, her favourite discipline.
Seizinger knows there is a long way to go before the title is decided, however.
"You have ups and downs in skiing. At the moment Wiberg is outstanding. It is a fair fight," the German said. "But I am proud of what I did today. It was a great result after my bad day yesterday."
